what_happened: The operator lifted the scope-guard pause on line 20261029-111202-2bpc by hand. The line had stopped twice in planning. Both stops came from mechanical plan-rule findings that used up planning rounds, and the second stop never reached the critic. Job d9y7 (landed as 198ffcf) now revises such findings without consuming a round. With the pause lifted, the next attempt gets all three critic rounds. The event lists no unmet criteria, findings or failed checks.
cause: The scope guard treats all spend on a line as one number. It does not record why an attempt stopped, so spend lost to a since-fixed Athena defect (mechanical plan-rule findings eating planning rounds) looks the same as a line that is truly running away. A fix to the cause does not reach the pause the old behavior already wrote. The pause is stored and never recomputed, so only an operator who notices and measures the cause can clear it. This is the fourth operator lift of the same kind.
prevention: Record a stop reason with each attempt's spend (environment, mechanical plan finding, real critic or verifier failure, producer failure). The guard should count only the reasons that signal runaway work. Store with each pause the rule version and the stop reasons that produced it. When a fix lands that changes which reasons count, or when a pause's cause is classified as non-counting, re-evaluate existing pauses automatically and lift those that no longer trip. Log each automatic lift so it is visible.
proposed_request: Make the scope guard classify the reason each attempt stopped and count only runaway-signal reasons toward a line's pause. Planning stops caused by mechanical plan-rule findings, and environment stops such as low disk, must not count. Store the counting-rule version and the per-attempt stop reasons in each pause record. On every drain start and after any landing that changes the counting rule, recompute every existing pause from its stored attempts. Lift automatically any pause that no longer trips, and write a record of the lift. Acceptance: (1) a test with a line whose only stops are mechanical plan-rule findings is not paused; (2) a test with a pause written under an older rule version is lifted on recompute when its stop reasons are non-counting; (3) a pause with real runaway reasons stays in force after recompute; (4) every automatic lift appears in the records with its reason.
